openings.subtype: lift landing door 900x2100, 2-panel centre-opening sliding (DOOR_LIFT_2_SOLID), lift 3
openings.evidence: A-DOOR block 'DOOR_LIFT_2_SOLID - 900x2100-3439061' (h 239F) ins (11.627,-44.440) rot 180 = the centre line of the 0.10 liner wall (top-level A-WALL hatch 5D8, y -44.49..-44.39) that hosts the door. Liner loops x 10.927..11.137 and 12.117..12.327 end at x=11.137 and x=12.117; door frame jambs x 11.137..11.177 and 12.077..12.117 sit against the liner ends; two leaves x 11.177..12.077 (0.90 clear) with opening arrows. The 0.25 thick core wall behind (A-WALL-PATT, y -44.24..-44.49) is open over the whole shaft width x 10.927..12.327 (1.40 = car frame, A-DETL 1.400 line).
openings.notes: Convention call: opening = the host liner-wall cut, frame included (0.98). The 1.40 m gap in the thick shaft wall is the shaft itself; the liners close it to 0.98, so nobody can pass through the other 0.42 m. Lifts 1 and 2 (x 5.81 and 8.72, west part) have the identical arrangement (liner hatches 5ED / 5E2, door blocks at the same y) and should use the same convention. Alternative if the key prefers the structural shaft gap: a=(10.927,-44.365) b=(12.327,-44.365) w=1.40.
openings.decision: All three versions have this door; they differ in the ends. A and E took the thick shaft wall gap (1.40, x 10.927/12.327 at y=-44.365); B took the gap between the jamb-return (liner) ends (0.98 at y=-44.44). I read the hatch loops and the block: the door is inserted on the liner's centre line (y=-44.44), the 0.10 liners fill the shaft front on the lobby face on both sides, and the frame jambs are flush with the liner ends, so the passage through the wall is 0.98 wide (frame included), not 1.40. Taken: a=(11.137,-44.44) b=(12.117,-44.44), w 0.98, wall 0.10.

method: Read the comparison packet (8 accepted, 5 disputes). Each dispute: rendered the spot at a 0.1 to 0.25 m grid with render.py and queried prims.pkl (hatch loops, door-block lines, glass-panel extents) to measure the ends; every accepted door re-checked against its glass-panel or wall-end extents. Missed-opening check: (1) all A-DOOR* items grouped by top-level handle in the box: 10 door blocks, all mapped to the 10 final openings; (2) shapely facing-wall-end analysis on all A-WALL / A-WALL-PATT / S-COLS hatch footprints (every pair of facing wall ends within 4.4 m): every hit explained (door gaps, closed stair gap, printer niche, corridor mouth, column boxes); (3) continuity walks along every glass partition and facade line: no doorless gaps; (4) scan for swing arcs on non-door layers: none; (5) whole-part render with a mark at every final opening plus three tiles: no unmarked door swing, leaf, sliding track or window band. Decided from the drawing, not by majority: lift 3 set to 0.98 (A and E had 1.40), L29E-09 centre line fixed at y=-50.116, three E-only items rejected, no opening added.
